text:
[LNUL.11.1] **A verb's argument may be `null`** — one absent value, not a
separate sentinel ([LNUL.7.1]). What each RHS verb does with a `null` argument:

| Verb | Policy |
|---|---|
| `log` | a `null` interpolated in the message renders as the empty string ([LGRA.2.9.6.2]) |
| `emit`, `publish` | a slot declared `T?` takes `null`, and any other slot raises a `TypeError` ([RARC.5.2.7]) |
| `call` | the call is not made, and the firing's other actions run ([NCBK.6.8]) |
| `cache` | **the stored value may be `null`, and it is stored as one** — caching that a thing was absent is a valid thing to cache |

**`cache` stores `null` as itself**, because a cache entry has no declared type
to refuse it. The consequence is deliberate: after this, a `cached(key)` **miss** and a stored
`null` are indistinguishable at the read ([LSTO.4.3.1a]). An author who needs to
tell them apart stores a sentinel of their own choosing.

**This table is over arguments to VERBS, and that is its whole scope.** A value
consumed as a boolean is ruled elsewhere and the two answers differ by site: a
`where` clause does not fire on `null` ([LNUL.4.3]); a guard admits on it
([LNUL.4.8]). Neither is a case of this clause.

A **fault** is not this. A fault raised while evaluating an argument never
reaches the verb, whichever verb holds the argument: the engine handles it as
[LERR.1.4] states, and a `ComputationError` or a `TypeError` abandons the
activation. A trap has no honest answer, is not an absent value, and
never reaches a slot ([LERR.1.4.9], [LCST.4.5.4]) — it abandons the activation
instead.

**Abandoning is a PREFIX rule, not a rollback.** A trap stops the action
sequence at the point it occurs: actions already performed **stand**, and
actions after it do not run. Nothing is undone, because a DS activation is
not atomic — the verbs have already reached the integrator's callbacks and the
engine has no way to recall them. So a rule that emits, then traps, then would
have published has emitted and not published, and the stream shows exactly that.

Stated because "abandons the activation" reads as though the activation leaves
no trace, and the half of it that already ran is the half an operator has to
reason about.

idris.name: Lnul_11_1__absent
idris.note: The clause's one absent value: a verb's argument is a value or `null`, and there is no second sentinel.

idris.name: Lnul_11_1__effect
idris.note: What a verb does with its argument: it proceeds on a value, and on `null` the outcome its row of the table states -- the empty string, the `null` in the slot, a `TypeError`, the call not made, the `null` stored.

idris.name: Lnul_11_1__outcome
idris.note: TWO absences where the clause states one -- Declared (a `null` that is data: the author wrote it, or stored it) and Missing (`cached(key)` never written, [LSTO.4.3.1], a statement about the store). Deliberately richer than the clause, whose one `null` they collapse to: the type exists to measure what the collapse loses.

idris.name: Lnul_11_1__slot
idris.note: The declared type of the slot an `emit` or a `publish` writes: `T?`, or any other. It is all the table's slot row reads.

idris.name: Lnul_11_1__verb
idris.note: The table's four rows: `log`; `emit` and `publish` as one row over the slot's declared type; `call`; `cache`.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__collapse
idris.note: The collapse the clause performs, as a function from the richer domain: Declared and Missing share the one `null`. Total and information-losing by construction; the theorem below measures what it loses.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__collapse_loses_the_miss
idris.note: NO IMPLEMENTATION CAN RECOVER THE DISTINCTION, not merely that this one does not. Quantified over every total function from the collapsed type and refuting all of them at once -- the shape an ITP is for, and why this is not in Alloy: a bounded search can exhibit a lossy encoding, but "no decoder exists" is a statement about a function space.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__is_a_miss
idris.note: A consumer the clause was NOT written for -- one that needs to know a store miss from a declared null. `ds.cache.cache_get` is `semidet` in the Mercury runtime precisely so a miss is not a value.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__null_raises_only_into_a_non_nullable_slot
idris.note: A `null` argument is an error in one row only: an `emit` or a `publish` into a slot not declared `T?` raises a `TypeError`. Every other row's outcome is not a fault. Over the table's rows, by cases.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__on_null
idris.note: The clause's table as a total function of the verb and its argument: `log` renders a `null` as the empty string, a slot declared `T?` takes it and any other slot raises a `TypeError`, `call` is not made, `cache` stores it. A transcription of the table; that every row answers is what the checker adds.

idris.name: lnul_11_1__stored_null_reads_as_a_miss
idris.note: The clause's sentence that a `cached(key)` miss and a stored `null` are indistinguishable at the read ([LSTO.4.3.1a]): the two collapse to one value. One `Refl`, the definition read back.
